components.description:
Electricity usage emissions from total site. Emission factor sourced from https://unfccc.int/documents/198197 on 2025-11-15. 

Note that the data here is an overestimate as in 2024 the JN dam was opened which now provides ~50% of the grid power and the data here is from 2021

As we cannot categorize the electricity consumption based on the production step (pre-processing, processing or post-processing), we have assigned all the electricity consumption to the Pyrolysis section.

Fuel used by diesel burnes to start up the machine. For stationary combustion of diesel in burners/boilers we apply a factor of 2.7 kgCO₂e per litre of diesel combusted (0.0027 tCO₂e/L). This is derived from the IPCC 2006 Guidelines default emission factors for gas/diesel oil in stationary combustion (74 100 kg CO₂/TJ, 3 kg CH₄/TJ, 0.6 kg N₂O/TJ) using standard diesel net calorific value and density. The resulting value is consistent with national GHG reporting factors such as the UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting, which give combustion-only diesel factors in the range 2.5–2.7 kgCO₂e per litre. 
As we cannot categorize the fuel consumption based on the production step (pre-processing, processing or post-processing), we have assigned all the fuel consumption to the Pyrolysis section.

Fuel used by diesel genset in case of power cuts. For stationary combustion of diesel in burners/boilers we apply a factor of 2.7 kgCO₂e per litre of diesel combusted (0.0027 tCO₂e/L). This is derived from the IPCC 2006 Guidelines default emission factors for gas/diesel oil in stationary combustion (74 100 kg CO₂/TJ, 3 kg CH₄/TJ, 0.6 kg N₂O/TJ) using standard diesel net calorific value and density. The resulting value is consistent with national GHG reporting factors such as the UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting, which give combustion-only diesel factors in the range 2.5–2.7 kgCO₂e per litre.
The amount of diesel is a conservative estimate. The logic of this estimate can be found in the source.
As we cannot categorize the fuel consumption based on the production step (pre-processing, processing or post-processing), we have assigned all the fuel consumption to the Pyrolysis section.

CO emissions from emissions test done during FAT, highest value converted to ppm and then 100% uncertainty applied.
The direct CO emissions will be assigned for each reporting period based on the amount of dry biomass used.
As the annual mass flow of the gas (36,792 t) is based on an estimated  amount of 17,520t of dry feedstock, the total mass flow for each reporting period will be assigned in the following way:
Reporting period mass flow = reporting period dry feedstock use (t) * (36,792 t/ 17,520 t).
